dedupe_keys.name: global fossil fuel supply chain network model

description: The Global Fossil Fuel Supply Chain model is published by Kruitwagen, Klaas, Baghaei Lakeh and Fan for asset-level transition-risk analysis. It constructs a geospatial network of coal, oil and gas infrastructure and estimates flows using minimum-cost routing. Inputs are asset inventories, demand estimates and transport connections; outputs are network flows and counterfactual demand or regional supply-shock results. The documented global network has 6.09 million nodes and 15.70 million edges, with annual demand estimates for population centres and power stations. Source is free under MIT; linked input collections retain their own terms. A limitation is that asset coverage, routing costs and aggregate trade calibration constrain the simulated flows. The model can assess energy infrastructure disruption and transition scenarios. OpenStreetMap (data-openstreetmap) is a documented input source. Public setup instructions describe the software dependencies. No graph database or input archive was downloaded.
